p: One of the best things about the Victoria Centre is just how much of Nottingham you can reach on foot. The Theatre Royal and Royal Concert Hall are only a short walk away, hosting touring shows, concerts and the famous Christmas panto, so a day of shopping can roll straight into an evening out. The tram stops nearby too, linking you to the station and further across the city.

Hockley, a few streets away, is Nottingham's independent quarter, packed with quirky shops, cafés and bars. It's a lovely contrast to the big chain stores, and a good place to find a more unusual gift. Close to the Lace Market, the National Justice Museum lets you explore the old courtroom and cells, and kids love the dressing-up and role-play side of it.

Underneath the city, the City of Caves takes you through sandstone caves that have been used for centuries, from tanneries to air-raid shelters, which is a fascinating way to spend an hour on a rainy afternoon.

Further out, Wollaton Hall, a grand Elizabethan mansion set in a deer park, is a short bus ride away and makes a great half-day trip with the kids. And if you're visiting in early October, Goose Fair, one of the country's oldest travelling fairs, takes over the Forest Recreation Ground with rides and stalls, bringing the whole city to life.
